ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.claim: The concluding discourse returns to the sūrah's opening theme: Qur'anic warnings are true, punishment signs can come, and prophetic histories already serve as signs for the stubborn Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p446/r5.anchor: Coming up are the concluding verses of the sūrah and the discourse links to its introductory part which is the real theme.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r3.claim: Most exegetes, including Ibn Abbas, understand the Prophet's rising as his rising for prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r3.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين منهم ابن عباس، على أن المعنى حين تقوم إلى الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r8.claim: An alternate gloss takes the Prophet's rising as private retreat by himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r8.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يراك قائما وساجدا. وقيل: معنى تقوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.claim: Ibn Atiyya says prayer is the apparent sense, though Mujahid and Qatada allow all the Prophet's activities and movements among worshippers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r10.anchor: ظاهر الآية أنه يريد قيام الصلاة، ويحتمل أن يريد سائر التصرفات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari pictures the Prophet praying at night and discreetly checking his companions' worship and inner states; after night prayer was abrogated, he toured their homes and heard their devotional murmuring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p197/r13.anchor: طاف تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون، بحرصه عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.claim: One interpretation is the Prophet’s night worship and his movement among the worshippers; “those prostrating” means the worshippers.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r5.anchor: المراد ما كان يفعله في جوف الليل من قيامه للتهجد

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.claim: An anonymous report says that after the night vigil ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet visited his Companions’ homes that night to see their worship, hearing them hum with remembrance like wasps in their nests; Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r6.anchor: كما يحكى أنه حين نسخ فرض قيام الليل طاف تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.claim: A second interpretation is that the Prophet rises to lead the congregation and moves among the worshippers in standing, bowing, prostration, and sitting.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r7.anchor: المعنى يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة وتقلبه في الساجدين تصرفه فيما بينهم

RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.claim: A third interpretation is that God never misses the Prophet’s state whenever he rises or moves among the worshippers while managing religious affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v24p148#3/r8.anchor: أنه لا يخفى عليه حالك كلما قمت وتقلبت مع الساجدين في كفاية أمور الدين

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.speaker: الرافضة
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.claim: The Rāfiḍa argue that the Prophet’s ancestors were believers and take the verse to allow God to have transferred his soul from one prostrating ancestor to another.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r1.anchor: الرافضة ذهبوا إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين وتمسكوا في ذلك بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.claim: The Rāfiḍa also cite the report that the Prophet was continually transferred from pure loins to pure wombs, reasoning that every unbeliever is impure; the verse is in 9:28. Rāzī gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r2.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( لم أزل أنقل من أصلاب الطاهرين إلى أرحام الطاهرات )

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.speaker: الرافضة
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.claim: To answer the reference to Abraham’s father Āzar, they say “father” can mean uncle: Jacob’s sons call Ishmael their father though he was their uncle, and the Prophet called al-ʿAbbās “my father.”
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r3.anchor: الرافضة ذهبوا إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين وتمسكوا في ذلك بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.speaker: الرافضة
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.claim: They also allow “father” to mean a maternal grandfather, citing Jesus’ inclusion among Abraham’s descendants although Abraham was his maternal grandfather.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r4.anchor: الرافضة ذهبوا إلى أن آباء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا مؤمنين وتمسكوا في ذلك بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.claim: Rāzī holds to the apparent sense of “his father Āzar”; the Rāfiḍa’s explanation shifts the word away from its apparent meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r5.anchor: بقوله تعالى : { لابيه ءازر } وما ذكروه صرف للفظ عن ظاهره

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.claim: Rāzī rejects taking the shared expression in all its possible senses at once, since an ambiguous word cannot carry all of them together.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r6.anchor: لما بينا أن حمل المشترك على كل معانيه غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.claim: The report about pure loins and wombs is a solitary report and therefore cannot outweigh the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v24p149/r7.anchor: وأما الحديث فهو خبر واحد فلا يعارض القرآن

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r3.claim: God’s seeing the Prophet explains the mercy promised: he should rely on the One who sees him.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r3.anchor: ثم أتبع به قوله : {الذى يريكم} إلخ لأنه كالسبب لتلك الرحمة أي توكل على من يراك

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r4.claim: Standing here means rising for night vigil prayer, the established religious usage of the term.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r4.anchor: {حين تقوم} أي إلى التهجد في جوف الليل فإن المعروف من القيام في العرف الشرعي إحياء الليل بالصلاة فيه.

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r5.claim: A prophetic report says the best prayer after the obligatory prayer is the night prayer.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أفضل الصلاة بعد الفريضة صلاة الليل".

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r6.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet never omitted night prayer, and when ill or tired he prayed sitting.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r6.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي عليه السلام "كان لا يدع قيام الليل وكان إذا مرض أو كسل صلى قاعدا".

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r7.claim: Muslim reports that when illness or another cause made the Prophet miss night prayer, he prayed twelve rakʿahs during the day in its place.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r7.anchor: ومنها "إذا فاتته الصلاة من الليل من وجع أو غيره صلى من النهار ثنتي عشرة ركعة" رواه "مسلم".

BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r8.claim: Tahajjud has special merit beyond other voluntary prayers, so missed prayer is made up even though ordinary supererogatory prayers are not.
BURSEVI:v6p227#2/r8.anchor: ما صلى عليه السلام في النهار بدل ما فات منه في الليل من ورد التهجد يدل على أن التهجد ليس كسائر النوافل

BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r7.claim: God sees the Prophet’s intention and resolve whenever he undertakes an affair; this awareness turns him from witnessing creatures and makes him watchful of hidden states.
BURSEVI:v6p227#3/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {الذى يرااك حين تقوم} أي يرى قصدك ونيتك وعزيمتك عند قيامك للأمور كلها

STUDYQURAN:26:218/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r1.speaker: one interpretation
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r1.claim: One interpretation takes standing as the night vigil prayer, considered by many to have been obligatory in Mecca before becoming supererogatory.
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r1.anchor: when thou standest [to pray] refers to the night vigil prayer

STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.speaker: another interpretation
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.claim: The phrase refers to the Prophet leading prayer and moving through bowing and prostration with the worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:26:218/r3.anchor: this refers to the Prophet’s role as leader of prayer, including his movements of bowing and prostrating

TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r3.claim: God sees the Prophet when he rises to pray.
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r3.anchor: يقول: الذي يراك حين تقوم إلى صلاتك.

TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says God sees the Prophet wherever he is.
TAB-FULL:v17p665#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {الذي يراك حين تقوم} [الشعراء: 218] قال: أينما كنت "

TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.claim: The apparent meaning is the Prophet's prayer: God sees him standing and moving among prostrating believers while leading them in congregational prayer.
TABATABAI:26:215-223/r5.anchor: والمراد بقرينة المقابلة القيام في الصلاة فيكون المعنى الذي يراك وأنت بعينه في حالتي قيامك وسجودك

TABRISI:26:215-219/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:215-219/r11.claim: God sees Muhammad when he rises from his sitting place or bed to pray, alone or with a congregation.
TABRISI:26:215-219/r11.anchor: أي الذي يبصرك حين تقوم من مجلسك أو فراشك إلى الصلاة وحدك وفي الجماعة

TABRISI:26:215-219/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:26:215-219/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says this means when Muhammad rises in prayer.
TABRISI:26:215-219/r12.anchor: معناه يراك حين تقوم في صلاتك عن ابن عباس.

TABRISI:26:215-219/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:215-219/r13.claim: Another explanation takes it as when Muhammad rises at night, unseen by others.
TABRISI:26:215-219/r13.anchor: حين تقوم بالليل لأنه لا يطلع عليه أحد غيره

TABRISI:26:215-219/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:215-219/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:215-219/r14.claim: A further explanation is when Muhammad rises to warn and perform the message.

THALABI:v7p183/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r6.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v7p183/r6.claim: Most commentators take “when you stand” to mean when Muhammad stands for prayer.
THALABI:v7p183/r6.anchor: الذي يراك حين تقوم إلى صلاتك عن أكثر المفسرين

THALABI:v7p183/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p183/r7.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p183/r7.claim: Mujahid says God sees Muhammad wherever he is and sees his changes of posture in prayer, standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating.
THALABI:v7p183/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الذي يراك أينما كنت وتقلبك ويرى تقلبك في صلاتك في حال قيامك وقعودك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r1.claim: They understand the rising as Muhammad’s rising for prayer and setting out to pray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r1.anchor: أي: للصلاة وإلى الصلاة. قاله ابن عباس والكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r2.claim: He reads the phrase as Muhammad rising alone to pray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: حين تقوم وحدك إلى الصلاة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r3.claim: God sees Muhammad wherever he is and whenever he rises.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الذي يراك أينما كنت، يعني: يراك حين تقوم أينما كنت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers Mujahid’s broad sense: every action Muhammad rises to is in God’s sight; the prayer-only readings highlight prayer’s importance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p140#3/r4.anchor: فعلى قول مجاهد: {تقوم} عام في كل شيء قام إليه، وهو الظاهر؛ لأنه بمرأى من الله إلى أي شيء قام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:218-219/r1.claim: The Prophet is seen when he stands for prayer.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r4.claim: Qatāda says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his conditions.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: الذي يراك قائما، وجالسا، وفي حالاتك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.claim: One view takes standing as praying alone and movement among prostrators as praying with the congregation; Yaḥyā says one of these two views is tafsīr of al-Ḥasan and Qatāda.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} [الشعراء: 218] في الصلاة وحدك {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] في صلاة الجميع.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.claim: Another view takes standing as the Prophet standing in prayer and movement among the prostrators as bowing and prostrating.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} [الشعراء: 218] في الصلاة قائما {وتقلبك في الساجدين} [الشعراء: 219] في الركوع والسجود.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r11.speaker: أبو مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r11.claim: Ibn Mujāhid transmits his father’s view that God sees the Prophet wherever he is.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p528/r11.anchor: وتفسير ابن مجاهد عن أبيه: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} [الشعراء: 218] أينما كنت.

QASHANI:26:218-219/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:218-219/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:218-219/r1.claim: God sees, accompanies, and preserves the Prophet as he rises through the minor resurrection, the intermediate primordial state, and the major resurrection in unity and steadfastness.
QASHANI:26:218-219/r1.anchor: في النشأة في القيامة الصغرى والفطرة في الوسطى بالوحدة حين الاستقامة في الكبرى

ELMALILI:26:213-223/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r8.claim: Standing may mean rising for prayer, especially the night vigil, or rising to enjoin right and exalt God's word.
ELMALILI:26:213-223/r8.anchor: namaza, bâhusus teheccüde veya emr bi’l-ma‘rûfa ve i‘lâ-yı kelimetullâha kalkarken seni

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.claim: Some commentators, as represented by Tabari, understand God seeing the Prophet as meaning that He sees him wherever he is.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:214/r7.anchor: “her nerede olursan ol seni gören” şeklinde yorumlamışlardır (Taberî, XIX, 123-125)

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r1.claim: Remain steady in absence and presence, knowing that you never escape the watch of divine power.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r1.anchor: قال : اثبت الراوية في حال الفقد والوجود لتعلم انك لم تغب عن ملاحظات القدرة .

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r2.speaker: الكتاني
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r2.claim: Reliance outwardly means following knowledge; inwardly and in its reality it means putting certainty into practice.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r2.anchor: سمعت محمد بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت الكتاني يقول التوكل في الظاهر ، والأصل اتباع العلم ،

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r3.speaker: أبو الحسين الرازي
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r3.claim: Reliance accompanies faith and matches its degree; seeking it requires preserving faith, disciplining the self by its rules, practicing patience, and seeking God's aid.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r3.anchor: سمعت محمد بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا الحسين الرازي يقول : التوكل مقرون مع الإيمان ، وكل إنسان توكله على قدر إيمانه

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r4.speaker: ابن عيينة
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r4.claim: Within the covenant of faith, reliance is the heart's dependence on God.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r4.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت محمد بن يعقوب الفرمي يقول : قال ابن عيينة : التوكل في عقد الإيمان اعتماد القلب على الله .

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r5.claim: Reliance is part of the covenant of faith, but its reality cannot be known through a description alone.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : التوكل في عقد الايمان ، ولا تعرف الحقيقة بالصفة .

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r6.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r6.claim: In contrast, Abu Sulayman al-Darani says he knows reliance only through its defining quality.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r6.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الداراني : أنا لا اعرف التوكل إلا بالصفة .

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r7.claim: Reliance is strength grounded in dependence and certainty.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم : التوكل هو القوة بالاعتماد واليقين .

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r8.claim: Reliance means dropping fear and hope in everyone besides God.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم : التوكل إسقاط الخوف والرجاء ممن سوى الله .

SULAMI:v2p82#3/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r9.claim: Reliance places the self in servanthood, attaches the heart to lordship, and directs one's whole gaze to God.
SULAMI:v2p82#3/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : التوكل طرح النفس في العبودية ، وتعلق القلب بالربوبية ، والنظر إلى الله بالكلية .

SAMIN-DURR:26:218/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:218/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:218/r1.claim: Alladhī yarāka may be nominative as predicate of an omitted subject, accusative as praise, or genitive as adjective, apposition, or explicative apposition.
SAMIN-DURR:26:218/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مرفوع المحل خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف، أو منصوبه على المدح

ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r1.speaker: Mujahid
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r1.claim: Mujahid, as quoted by Tabari, interprets God's seeing Muhammad when he stands as wherever he may be.
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r1.anchor: According to Mujahid (as quoted by Tabari), this means "wherever thou mayest be".

ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r2.speaker: Other commentators
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r2.claim: Other commentators limit the phrase to standing for prayer; Asad rejects this as too narrow compared with Mujahid's broader reading.
ASAD-NOTES:26:214#n95/r2.anchor: Other commentators take it to mean "when thou standest up for prayer", but this seems to be too narrow an interpretation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r2.claim: God watches the Prophet's night prayer and supplication, as well as his efforts to help companions share in its blessings, and will account for these deeds and aid him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r2.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is also in God’s notice when he tries that his companions also reap the blessings of the night prayer and supplication.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r3.speaker: Exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r3.claim: Exegetes offer various possible interpretations of “when you get up,” though the passage does not specify their alternatives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r3.anchor: Out exegetes have presented various opinions in the interpretation of the expression “when you get up” and each can be possible.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r4.claim: The author prefers reading the Prophet's getting up as rising for tahajjud, with the reference to his movement among prostrators providing a strong indication.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r4.anchor: in my opinion, the correct opinion among these is the one which says that this getting up relates to getting up for the tahajjud prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.claim: The Gospels similarly describe Jesus praying on a mountain during trial, urging disciples to stay awake, and repeatedly waking them to supplicate for protection.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p455/r7.anchor: Jesus (sws) went to the mountains and busied himself in supplications and also asked his disciples to remain awake and pray to God

ALUSI-FULL:v19p137/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p137/r1.claim: The phrase means that God sees the Prophet when he rises to pray.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r4.claim: Most exegetes say God sees Muhammad when he stands for prayer.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r5.claim: Mujahid says God sees Muhammad wherever he is.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الذي يراك أينما كنت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p134/r6.claim: Another view is that God sees Muhammad standing to call people to Islam.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r3.claim: His standing is for the night vigil prayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r3.anchor: الذي يراك حين تقوم } إلى التهجد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.claim: God’s awareness of the Prophet’s deserving state follows the promise of power over enemies and support for allies, affirming reliance and reassuring his heart.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:217-219/r7.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله تعالى بعلمه بحاله التي بها يستأهل ولايته بعد وصفه بأن من شأنه قهر أعدائه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.claim: The description following the trust command establishes God’s sufficiency: His encompassing knowledge secures every benefit and repels every harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r15.anchor: بما يقتضي الكفاية في كل ما ينوب من دفع الضر وجلب النفع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r16.claim: God sees the Prophet with sight and knowledge as he rises from bed after sleep, leaving its comfort for God’s pleasure.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p397/r16.anchor: من نومك من فرشك تاركا لحبك , لأجل رضا ربك

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet is seen when he rises for prayer.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: للصلاة

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says the phrase covers rising from one's bed or one's seat.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: من فراشك أو من مجلسك

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r3.claim: Mujahid says God sees the Prophet wherever he is.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: أينما كنت

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r4.claim: Saʿid b. Jubayr says the Prophet is seen in his prayer.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r4.anchor: عن سعيد ابن جبير {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: في صلاتك

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the Prophet's movements as standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: قيامه وركوعه وسجوده وجلوسه

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.claim: Qatada says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his states; his turning includes standing, bowing, prostrating, and sitting.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: يراك قائما وقاعدا وعلى حالاتك {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: قيامه وركوعه وسجوده وجلوسه

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.claim: Qatada says God sees the Prophet alone in prayer and sees him among the congregation.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {الذي يراك حين تقوم} قال: يراك قائما وقاعدا وعلى حالاتك {وتقلبك في الساجدين} قال: في الصلاة يراك وحدك ويراك في الجميع

DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the two phrases as the Prophet's standing, bowing, and prostrating.
DURR-FULL:v6p330/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس {الذي يراك حين تقوم وتقلبك في الساجدين} يقول: قيامك وركوعك وسجودك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains standing as rising for prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r1.anchor: ابن عباس في قول الله : الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : تقوم الصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r2.claim: Ikrima says God sees the Prophet's standing, bowing, and prostration.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r2.anchor: عكرمة في قول الله : الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : يرى قيامه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r3.claim: Hasan says this refers to when the Prophet prays alone.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r3.anchor: الحسن يقول في قول الله : الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : حين تقوم اذا صليت وحدك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says this means rising from bed or from one's seat.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r4.anchor: الضحاك الذي يراك حين تقوم قال : حين تقوم من فراشك

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r5.claim: Ikrima says God sees the Prophet standing and sitting among the people.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r5.anchor: عكرمة قال : الذي يراك حين تقوم معهم وتقعد

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r6.claim: Qatada says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his states.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r6.anchor: قتادة قوله : الذي يراك حين تقوم يقول : الذي يراك قائما

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r7.claim: Mujahid says God sees the Prophet wherever he is.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد : يراك حين تقوم اينما كنت

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r8.claim: Hasan gives another gloss: when the Prophet is alone in private prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2827#4/r8.anchor: الحسن يقول : الذي يراك حين تقوم حين تخلو بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r7.claim: The description means God's special care: He sees the Prophet turning toward Him and accepts that devotion, like the expression in 52:48.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r7.anchor: رؤية خاصة وهي رؤية الإقبال والتقبل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r8.claim: The Prophet's standing refers to prayer during the middle of the night, an established Quranic usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r8.anchor: غلب هذا الاسم عليه في اصطلاح القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.claim: The compact pairing conveys care for Muslims alongside care for their Messenger, presenting that as part of his blessing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p203/r10.anchor: يجمع معنى العناية بالمسلمين تبعا للعناية برسولهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r3.claim: يراك means “perceives you”; the apparent reference is to standing in prayer, though it may mean all of Muḥammad's activities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r3.anchor: وظاهر الآية أراد قيام الصلاة، ويحتمل أن يريد سائر التصرفات وهو تأويل مجاهد وقتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda allow the verse to refer to Muḥammad's activities generally, not just prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p245#2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد سائر التصرفات وهو تأويل مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say “when you rise” means when you rise to pray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r1.anchor: حين تقوم إلى الصلاة قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r2.speaker: أبو الجوزاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r2.claim: Abū al-Jawzāʾ says it means when you rise from your place.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r2.anchor: حين تقوم من مقامك قاله أبو الجوزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p148#3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means when you are alone.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r2.claim: God's seeing the Prophet when he rises means that God attends to and cares for him, as also expressed in 52:48.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r2.anchor: أي: هو معتن بك، كما قال تعالى: {واصبر (3) لحكم ربك فإنك بأعيننا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the Prophet's rising as his rising to pray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {الذي يراك حين تقوم} يعني: إلى الصلاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says God sees the Prophet standing, bowing, and prostrating.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: يرى قيامه وركوعه وسجوده.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the phrase refers to the Prophet praying alone.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes it to mean rising from the bed or from a sitting place.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {الذي يراك حين تقوم.} أي: من فراشك أو مجلسك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r7.claim: Qatāda says God sees the Prophet standing, sitting, and in all his states.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p171/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: {الذي يراك} : قائما وجالسا وعلى حالاتك.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.claim: Mention of God's mercy leads into the Prophet's night worship and his attentive inspection of companions' worship and preparation for the afterlife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r7.anchor: ثم اتبع كونه رحيما على رسوله ما هو من أسباب الرحمة : وهو ذكر ما كان يفعله في جوف الليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.claim: A report says that after night prayer ceased to be obligatory, the Prophet toured his companions' homes and heard remembrance and recitation buzzing like hornets' nests.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r8.anchor: كما يحكى أنه حين نسخ فرض قيام الليل ، طاف تلك الليلة ببيوت أصحابه لينظر ما يصنعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.speaker: some
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.claim: Another explanation is that God sees the Prophet rise to lead congregational prayer and move among worshippers in its positions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r10.anchor: وقيل : معناه يراك حين تقوم للصلاة بالناس جماعة . وتقلبه في الساجدين : تصرفه فيما بينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.claim: The phrase may mean God sees the Prophet whenever he rises and moves among worshippers while managing religious affairs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p346/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أنه : لا يخفى عليه حالك كلما قمت وتقلبت مع الساجدين في كفاية أمور الدين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says this refers to the Prophet rising for prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : حين تقوم في الصلاة , قاله ابن عباس . الثاني : حين تقوم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says it refers to rising from bed or from a sitting place.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : حين تقوم من فراشك ومجلسك ، قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r3.claim: Qatada takes the phrase to mean that God sees the Prophet in all his states, standing and sitting.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : يعني قائما وجالسا وعلى حالاتك كلها , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says it refers to when the Prophet is alone; standing is used to indicate the solitude reached by rising away from others.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r4.anchor: الرابع : يعني حين تخلو , قاله الحسن , ويكون القيام عبارة عن الخلوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.claim: Qatada distinguishes solitary prayer at the first phrase from congregational prayer at the second.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r10.anchor: السادس : أن معنى قوله { الذي يراك حين تقوم } إذا صليت منفردا { وتقلبك في الساجدين } إذا صليت في الجماعة , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.claim: He suggests that the first phrase may refer to the Prophet rising to fight the polytheists and the second to his affairs among Muslims and the religious rulings he establishes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p188#2/r11.anchor: ويحتمل سابعا : الذي يراك حين تقوم لجهاد المشركين , { وتقلبك في الساجدين } فيما تريد به المسلمين

MUQATIL:26:215-220/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:215-220/r5.claim: God sees the Prophet when he rises alone to pray.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p200#10/r1.claim: The Prophet is seen when he rises for night prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r11.claim: Most commentators take “when you rise” to mean rising for prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r11.anchor: { الذي يراك حين تقوم } أي حين تقوم إلى الصلاة في قول أكثر المفسرين: ابن عباس وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r12.claim: Mujāhid understands it as whenever and wherever the Prophet rises.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:214-220/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يعني حين تقوم حيثما كنت
